sources.entry: OpenCode - Open-source terminal AI coding agent with skills, MCP, and custom workflows. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that runs in the terminal and is also offered as a beta desktop app.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents OpenCode as an open-source AI coding agent and lists many install routes: an install script, npm, brew, pacman, AUR, mise, and Nix. It ships a desktop app (beta) with downloads for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows, and Linux. It includes two built-in agents that can be switched with the Tab key: "build", a default full-access agent for development work, and "plan", a read-only agent that denies file edits by default and asks permission before running bash commands. A "general" subagent handles complex searches and multistep tasks and can be invoked with @general. The README points to external docs for configuration and to a contributing guide. It also asks projects that use "opencode" in their names to state they are not affiliated with the OpenCode team.
use_cases: exploring an unfamiliar codebase safely in read-only mode
planning code changes before editing files
running multistep development tasks with an AI agent
installing a coding agent on macOS, Linux, or Windows
stack: JavaScript package managers (npm, bun, pnpm, yarn)
notable: Read-only plan agent that denies edits by default and asks before bash commands
Switch between build and plan agents with the Tab key
Many install channels including Homebrew, Arch AUR, Nix, and mise
Available as a desktop app (beta) for macOS, Windows, and Linux
README translated into more than 20 languages
caveats: The README advises removing versions older than 0.1.x before installing
The official brew formula is updated less often than the opencode-v2 tap, according to the README
The README does not state a license
keywords: use ai to write code in terminal
let an ai agent edit my files
